articles.title: Centrist Democrats Are Trying to Throw the Michigan Race
articles.author: Branko Marcetic
articles.content_excerpt: In Michigan, where progressive Abdul El-Sayed is facing off for the must-win Senate seat against Donald Trump–backed Mike Rogers, Democrats have a problem. How to reconcile their distaste for their own party’s nominee with the imperative to care about winning? Attorney General Dana Nessel modeled a way out of the bind with a comically backhanded endorsement. Tasked with trying to convince Jewish Democrats that they should vote for El-Sayed despite the blizzard of smears charging he’s a dangerous antisemite, Attorney General Dana Nessel offered the most unappetizing of unappetizing pitches. articles.title: The Dog Stars Is a Western in Postapocalyptic Drag
articles.author: Eileen Jones
articles.content_excerpt: The dullest yet most enraging film of the year may very well be The Dog Stars , a draggy postapocalyptic thriller with no thrills, even of the grim dystopian kind. This latest effort by director Ridley Scott, from a screenplay by Mark L. Smith ( Twisters, The Revenant ) based on the 2012 novel of the same name by Peter Heller, is about the survivors of a flu pandemic who live in isolated enclaves defending their turf from marauding bands of desperate nomads. Jacob Elordi plays Hig, an ex-mechanic turned prop pilot whose last remaining relationship from the old days is with his dog, Jasper. Jasper is a cool dog, a Belgian Malinois, who keeps whining nervously as if he knows he’s not safe with Hig. articles.title: The Scandal That Could Break the Latin American Far Right
articles.author: Kurt Hackbarth
articles.content_excerpt: On Tuesday, August 18, an Argentine citizen named Fernando Cerimedo was arrested at the Viru Viru International Airport in Santa Cruz de la Sierra, Bolivia. Cerimedo, age forty-five, was charged with the attempted homicide of his ex-partner, Bolivian lawyer Nadia Beller, and ordered held for 180 days of pretrial detention. The details are grisly: security camera footage showed hit men, disguised as delivery workers, firing on an unsuspecting Beller at point-blank range before fleeing the scene. Compounding matters, Beller, who miraculously survived the assault, was apparently pregnant with Cerimedo’s own child. articles.title: The Human Soul of the Fight to Control AI
articles.author: Daniele G. Palmer
articles.content_excerpt: During World War II, bomber pilots would tell each other, “if you’re taking flak, you’re over the target.” Don’t demur, you’ve struck a nerve. Opposition, at times, isn’t all that bad a sign — if anything, it could point to something good, or at least true. Judged by that standard, the reception of Pope Leo XIV’s pronouncement on artificial Intelligence has been curious. Some have fought over its account of just war theory; others have questioned its denial of machine sentience. Yet its diagnosis of the politics AI relies on, and the fixes needed to guard against it, has gone almost entirely unchallenged, especially among technologists. articles.title: The Israel Lobby Is Out of Control
articles.author: Eli Clifton
articles.content_excerpt: In a year of record-breaking campaign spending by the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) and widespread popular revulsion at Donald Trump’s war on Iran, a deeply researched study of the Israel lobby couldn’t be timelier. Jacobin ’s Seth Ackerman spoke with investigative journalist Eli Clifton and veteran scholar Ian Lustick about their new book Israel’s Lobby : America in the Grip of a Foreign Power , which reveals how the lobby has not only warped Washington politics but accelerated Israel’s own ideological radicalization — and now threatens Americans’ civil liberties at home. articles.title: Volunteers Were the Key to NYC-DSA’s Socialist Sweep
articles.author: Ashley Bishop
articles.content_excerpt: Since the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) swept the New York primaries in June, conservative and liberal media alike have tried to make sense of DSA’s meteoric rise by tying them to ascendant New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and his “kingmaking” abilities. Beyond a cursory nod to the army of volunteers knocking doors and making phone calls, far less has been made of the why behind the volunteer effort that propelled these candidates to victory. Across NYC-DSA’s slate of endorsed candidates, roughly 8,500 volunteers showed up to knock more than 750,000 doors, with over 810,000 attempted door knocks — for an off-year electoral cycle. articles.title: HBO’s Burning Man Documentary Omits the Festival’s Workers
articles.author: Keith A. Spencer
articles.content_excerpt: It’s been a precarious decade for Burning Man. The legendary counterculture gathering was canceled two years in a row due to COVID-19 and has yet to recover its record pre-pandemic attendance numbers. In 2023, the indulgent spectacle was marred by sensational headlines about attendees being trapped by torrential downpours that snared vehicles in mud. Moreover, the past decade has seen a parade of negative headlines about Burning Man — including stories of horrific volunteer injuries and a pattern of worker suicides . It’s a weighty moment to release a new documentary series about Burning Man. Directed by Jehane Noujaim and Vikram Gandhi and shot over five years, the four-part docuseries The Man Will Burn dropped its final episode on HBO on July 30.
